findings.title: Four flights were randomized but analyzed as 159 people
findings.description: Methods assigned two female flights to each briefing arm, then compared injuries and survey items with a person-level chi-squared test. With only two clusters per arm, any shared flight-level injury risk (drill instructors, barracks, training load) makes the reported MSKI p=.047 and BSI p=.037 anti-conservative. Those two p-values are the basis for the abstract's 43% and 66% relative risk reductions. A cluster-level analysis cannot be reconstructed because flight-level counts are not printed.

adjudication.rationale: Flights, not people, were randomized (two per briefing arm), yet MSKI p=.047 and BSI p=.037 are person-level Pearson chi-squares on 25/80 vs 14/79 and 12/80 vs 4/79. Those p-values underpin the abstract's 43% and 66% relative reductions. With two clusters per arm the tests are anti-conservative; a valid cluster analysis is essentially unidentified. Limitation (1) noted block randomization but did not change the analysis.

findings.title: Title credits MVI compliance; both arms received the MVI
findings.description: The title states that multivitamin compliance reduces injuries. The randomized contrast is briefing modality (video versus video plus in-person SME brief). Both cohorts received the same prenatal MVI. No unsupplemented control and no mediation test of compliance are reported. The Discussion infers that the brief improved compliance which in turn reduced injuries. That causal chain is not identified by the design, which the authors themselves list as limitation (2).

findings.title: Table III survey percentages cannot come from n=80 and n=79
findings.description: Table III headers are n=80 and n=79 (total 159), but reconstruct_2x2 finds no column split summing to 159 that produces the paired survey percentages (daily MVI 14.86 vs 34.25, most days 37.84 vs 63.01, never 20.27 vs 8.22, found-brief-effective 95.89 vs 98.63). Unique recovered bases (video compliance 11/74, 28/74, 15/74; in-person 25/73, 46/73, 6/73; brief items on n=73) also reproduce the printed Pearson p-values (.0063, .0023, .037, .007). Methods still state that all trainees completed questionnaires. Compliance contrasts remain; the printed denominators and completeness claim do not.

findings.title: Table III medical-hold 1.27% is not attainable at n=80
findings.description: Medical hold is printed as 1.27% in both columns, under headers n=80 and n=79, with p=.99. Reconstruct_2x2 finds no 2x2 whose column totals sum to 159 and that reproduces both 1.27% values at two decimals. Results state there were no losses of routinely collected data, so the injury/training denominators should be 80 and 79. One event in 79 is 1.27%; one event in 80 is 1.25%, which would print as 1.25 not 1.27. The video-only cell matches the in-person value rather than n=80. Recycle-fitness 2.50% and 2.53% do match 2/80 and 2/79.

findings.title: Table I lists vitamin C as 100 μg at 83% daily value
findings.description: Table I prints vitamin C (ascorbic acid) as 100 μg and 83% daily value for pregnant and lactating women. NIH ODS RDAs for vitamin C are in milligrams: 85 mg in pregnancy and 120 mg in lactation. 100 mg of 120 mg is 83%, matching the printed percent; 100 μg of 120 mg is 0.08%. Typical prenatal labels use 100 mg ascorbic acid. Adjacent rows correctly use μg for vitamins A, D, folate, and B12 and mg for iron, calcium, and zinc, so the vitamin C unit is a 1000-fold error relative to the printed %DV.

findings.title: Reference 8 does not support the 22 mg iron claim
findings.description: The Introduction states that 27 mg of iron approximates the estimated 22 mg daily requirement for females in military training and cites reference 8. Reference 8 is Martineau et al., BMJ 2017, an IPD meta-analysis of vitamin D for acute respiratory tract infections. It does not estimate iron requirements. The paper's own reference 17 (IOM mineral requirements for military personnel) is the work that would support a training-adjusted iron figure.

findings.title: Printed ages contradict the no-difference claim
findings.description: Results state that no significant differences in age or BMI were detected. Table II prints age 21±3 years (n=80) versus 23±5 (n=79). check_effect_plausibility on those printed means and SDs gives d=-0.48, 95% CI [-0.80, -0.17], which excludes zero. An equal-variance t on the same inputs is t=-3.06, df=157, p=0.0026. BMI 24.1±2.6 versus 24.0±2.8 is compatible with no difference (p=0.82). Age is printed to zero decimals, so unrounded means could be closer; the printed figures as they stand do not support the no-difference sentence.

findings.title: Stated power analysis cannot produce n=77 per cohort
findings.description: Methods say alpha 0.05, power 0.99, and a 25% relatively greater daily MVI compliance yielded 77 trainees per cohort. A two-proportion calculation at power 0.99 for a 25% relative increase needs hundreds to thousands per arm across baselines 0.15-0.50 (e.g. 0.15 vs 0.1875 needs n=3655). Even at the conventional power 0.80 the same relative effect needs n=1562 at baseline 0.15. A 25 percentage-point increase at power 0.80 gives n=48-60, nearer 77, so the printed 'relatively greater' and 'power of 0.99' jointly do not produce the stated sample size.
findings.quote: a power analysis calculation was completed using α≤ 0.05 for the significance level, a power of 0.99. We estimated a 25% relatively greater daily MVI compliance in trainees receiving the in-person brief compared to those viewing the video alone, which yielded a need for each cohort to have 77 trainees to demonstrate a significant difference.

anchors.label: Methods, power analysis
anchors.quote: a power analysis calculation was completed using α≤ 0.05 for the significance level, a power of 0.99. We estimated a 25% relatively greater daily MVI compliance in trainees receiving the in-person brief compared to those viewing the video alone, which yielded a need for each cohort to have 77 trainees to demonstrate a significant difference.

findings.anchor_problem: None. Single contiguous Methods power-analysis sentence.nputs

adjudication.rationale: Methods say alpha 0.05, power 0.99, and a 25% relatively greater daily MVI compliance yielded n=77 per cohort. A two-proportion calculation at those inputs needs thousands per arm for a 25% relative lift from a 0.15 baseline (h≈0.10 → about 3675/group). n=77 per group at 99% power corresponds to a large h≈0.70, which the stated 25% relative change does not produce. The enrolled squadron was not sized by that calculation.

findings.title: BSI 66% relative reduction exceeds the Lappe Ca-D trial
findings.description: The paper reports a 66% relative and 10% absolute reduction in BSI (15% vs 5.06%) after a briefing that changed self-reported daily MVI use from 14.86% to 34.25%. Both arms received the same tablet (400 IU vitamin D and 200 mg calcium). Lappe et al., cited as the dose benchmark, randomized 5201 female Navy recruits to 2000 mg calcium plus 800 IU vitamin D versus placebo and found a 20% ITT reduction (5.3% vs 6.6%). Cohen's d on the reconstructed BSI proportions is 0.33 (95% CI 0.02-0.65), within usual medicine-RCT range; the relative-risk comparison to Lappe is the implausible piece. Magnitude is capped at suspicious.

adjudication.rationale: The 66% relative BSI reduction (15% vs 5.06%) is the briefing contrast, not a supplement-versus-placebo effect; both arms received 400 IU vitamin D and 200 mg calcium. Relative to Lappe et al., cited as the dose benchmark, attributing that reduction to a modest compliance increment is a mechanistic-plausibility note, not an arithmetic error in the printed rates.

adjudication.summary: The abstract’s significant MSKI and BSI reductions (p=.047 and p=.037; 43% and 66% relative reductions) are person-level chi-squared tests after randomizing four flights, two per arm. Those p-values match unadjusted Pearson tests on 25/80 versus 14/79 MSKI and 12/80 versus 4/79 BSI. With two clusters per arm the tests are anti-conservative, and a valid cluster analysis is essentially unidentified. Table III survey percentages such as daily MVI 14.86% versus 34.25% cannot be produced from n=80 and n=79; they and the printed p-values match recovered item n of 74 and 73, contrary to the claim that all trainees completed questionnaires. Medical-hold 1.27% is impossible at n=80 (R GRIM). Printed ages 21±3 versus 23±5 contradict the no-difference claim (d=−0.48, CI −0.80 to −0.17). Injury percentages at the stated n, their Pearson p-values, BMI, and the n=80+79 flow do reconcile. The title credits MVI compliance although both arms received the same tablet. A corrigendum should qualify or withdraw the injury significance claims, print survey denominators, and correct the age sentence, medical-hold cell, and title. Nothing here established intent.

Trainees were not told they were in a randomized experiment; IRB number FWH20220101E is given as exempt QI. Disclosed, so not a withheld-ethics finding; journal ethics of publishing that design is outside this beat.

rounding_convention.note: Values that fail the round-half convention but are consistent if the reporter TRUNCATES (SPSS's default, and several journal styles). NOT a finding and never counted as one: a single instance is a house style. The RATE is the signal -- this class of anomaly is commoner in papers with more serious problems, so a high proportion is grounds to look harder, not evidence in itself.

grace.reading: Nothing needed an allowance; every item reconciled on its printed values.

sd_convention.note: Values that fail under the sample (Bessel, n-1) SD but are consistent under the POPULATION (n) SD -- numpy's std default and Excel's STDEVP. NOT a finding and never counted as one: choosing a convention is not fabrication. The RATE is the signal, on the same reasoning as the rounding convention above.

harness_sweep.why: These checks were aimed by the harness, not by the model: every eligible target in the paper's tables was enumerated and checked. That makes their coverage identical from run to run, which the model-aimed checks are not -- two runs of this pipeline on one paper overlapped on 0 of 10 model-aimed targets.
